summary: AI observability tools give teams visibility into how LLM applications behave in production by tracing requests, evaluating output quality, and tracking token usage and costs. As LLM-powered features scale, trace-heavy workloads can add 5–10% on top of underlying API spend, making observability essential for controlling costs, debugging failures, and maintaining output quality. Choosing the right tool helps balance tracing depth, evaluation capabilities, and pricing for your specific workload.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: End-to-end traces of LLM chains and agents, token usage, latency, cost, and evaluation metrics for applications (especially those built with LangChain).
features: Distributed tracing with span hierarchies for chains and agents
Dataset and evaluation suite (LLM-as-judge and custom evals)
tools.pricing: Free developer tier; LangSmith Plus around $264 per 100,000 traces with 14-day base data retention. Trace costs typically run ~5–10% of underlying LLM API spend for trace-heavy workloads. Enterprise plans available.
tools.best_for: Teams building with LangChain/LangGraph that need deep tracing, prompt iteration, and integrated evaluation.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests via a proxy/gateway: cost per request, token usage, latency, caching, and usage analytics across providers.
features: One-line proxy integration for OpenAI and other providers
Cost and usage tracking with per-user/per-model breakdowns
tools.pricing: Free tier with 10,000 requests/month; usage-based pricing roughly $79 per 100,000 traces with 30 days of data retention (notably cheaper and longer retention than LangSmith Plus).
tools.best_for: Teams wanting a lightweight, low-cost, provider-agnostic proxy focused on cost tracking and caching.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
tools.monitors: LLM and ML experiment runs, model performance, traces (via W&B Weave), token usage, latency, and evaluation results.
features: W&B Weave for LLM tracing and evaluation
tools.pricing: Free tier for individuals; team and enterprise plans are usage/seat-based with custom enterprise pricing.
tools.best_for: ML and research teams who want unified experiment tracking plus LLM observability in one platform.

tools.name: Arize AI
tools.monitors: Production LLM and ML model performance, drift, embeddings, traces, evaluations, and data quality at scale.
features: LLM tracing and evaluation (Arize Phoenix open-source companion)
Drift, data quality, and embedding monitoring
Automated performance alerts and root-cause analysis
Support for RAG and agent observability
tools.pricing: Free open-source Phoenix tier; AX platform offers a free tier with paid Pro and custom Enterprise plans.
tools.best_for: Enterprises needing production-grade monitoring, drift detection, and evaluation for both ML and LLM systems.

tools.name: LangFuse
tools.monitors: LLM application traces, nested spans, token usage, cost, latency, prompt performance, and evaluation scores.
features: Open-source tracing with nested span hierarchies
Cost and token tracking per trace
tools.pricing: Open-source and self-hostable for free; managed cloud offers a free Hobby tier, with Core/Pro and Enterprise plans based on usage.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting an open-source, self-hostable, framework-agnostic observability and evaluation platform.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM calls, vector DB queries, and framework operations via OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation, exporting traces/metrics to your chosen backend.
features: Vendor-neutral traces exportable to any OTel backend
Auto-instrumentation for popular LLM SDKs and vector DBs
Integrates with Traceloop and existing observability stacks
tools.pricing: Free and open-source (Apache 2.0); costs come only from the backend/platform you export data to (e.g., Traceloop managed plans).
tools.best_for: Engineering teams that want standards-based, vendor-neutral instrumentation plugged into existing observability tooling.

cost_tips: Cache repeated or similar prompts and responses (e.g., via Helicone or a semantic cache) to avoid paying for redundant LLM calls.
Route requests to the smallest model that meets quality requirements, reserving expensive frontier models for genuinely hard tasks.
Trim prompt and context size—remove boilerplate, compress retrieved context, and cap max output tokens to reduce per-request token spend.
Monitor usage per feature, user, and model to catch runaway costs early, set budget alerts, and factor in that trace-heavy observability can add 5–10% on top of base API spend.
